title: Getting Started with Marketing in Strawberry
description: Connect audience evidence, campaign planning, content, and performance learning without losing the brand or the reasoning between steps.
introduction: Marketing often breaks at the handoffs. Audience research becomes a slide nobody uses. A campaign plan loses its evidence when production starts. Performance arrives later as a dashboard with no memory of why the work looked that way.

Strawberry can keep those steps connected. The same companion can work across the visible browser, logged-in marketing tools, customer evidence, documents, meetings, and the live web. It can remember the team's accepted sources, brand judgment, and corrections, then carry them from one useful result into the next.

blocks.text: You do not need to build the whole system before beginning. Bring the product, audience, campaign, content, search, or performance question that matters now. Strawberry can recommend a few relevant starting points and complete one result the team can review while keeping the larger system visible.

items.context: Choose and complete the marketing workflow that would help most right now.

blocks.text: Because the work happens beside your real tabs and logged-in tools, you can inspect the sources, coach the judgment, take over when needed, and decide whether a draft should become an external action.

sections.title: Begin with audience evidence, then make the campaign decision

blocks.text: Good audience work joins qualitative and quantitative evidence without pretending every source represents the same population. Interviews, support conversations, reviews, communities, search behavior, analytics, and campaign data can reveal needs, language, behavior, channels, and tensions. Strawberry keeps representative examples and links close to the synthesis, along with the gaps and confidence behind it.

An accepted audience view can become a campaign plan with a clear objective, proposition, offer, channel roles, asset needs, owners, dependencies, measurement, and risks. Planning stops before platform configuration, launch, or spend changes, so the team approves the strategy before operational momentum makes it harder to correct.

sections.title: Connect the plan to content people can use

blocks.text: A content plan should explain why each theme and format exists, which evidence supports it, who owns it, and how the work can be reused. It should also respect the team's actual capacity. Filling a calendar is not the same as making a plan.

When a brief is ready, Strawberry can create the anchor asset and adapt its idea across articles, email, social, landing pages, and similar formats. Repurposing changes the structure, depth, proof, and call to action for the channel; it does not simply make the same copy shorter. Substantial visual work and publishing remain their own steps.

items.context: Turn the strategy and evidence into themes, briefs, owners, cadence, and reuse.
Create source-grounded content and useful channel-specific variants.

sections.title: Measure without pretending attribution is clean

blocks.text: Marketing performance becomes easier to act on when definitions come before conclusions. Strawberry can reconcile periods, currencies, funnel stages, attribution windows, and source quality, then show which audience, channel, message, creative, or operational change may explain the result.

Observed change, plausible explanation, and recommendation remain separate. One platform's model is not treated as ground truth, and a before-and-after chart is not automatically a causal result. When extraction, joins, statistical work, or validation becomes substantial, shared Data capabilities can handle that layer while Marketing keeps the interpretive judgment.

items.context: Reconcile the evidence, explain the changes that matter, and recommend the next decision or experiment.

sections.title: Use specialists at the real branches

blocks.text: Competitor analysis and SEO remain focused workflows because they bring their own sources and judgment. Agency work adds client separation, briefing, delivery, and reporting boundaries rather than changing the underlying Marketing method. After an in-house workflow has worked, Operations can help turn the accepted sources, owners, destination, privacy rules, and review behavior into a shared team process.

Keep external actions distinct. Research does not approve contact-list building. A campaign plan does not approve launch. Copy approval does not approve publishing, sending, CMS changes, tracking changes, or spend. Strawberry follows the active permission for the exact account, destination, action, and conditions, and verifies work it completes.
